questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a galaxy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andromeda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andromeda** is a spiral galaxy located approximately **2.537 million light-years** from Earth. It is the closest large galaxy to the Milky Way.
 
• It is also known as **M31**, Messier 31, or NGC 224, and is part of the Local Group of galaxies, which includes the Milky Way, Triangulum, and around 54 other smaller galaxies.
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy is massive, containing approximately **one trillion stars**, which is more than twice the number of stars in the Milky Way.
 
• It is visible to the naked eye from Earth in areas with dark skies and is often studied to understand galaxy formation, structure, and dynamics.
 
• Unlike stars, constellations, or star systems, galaxies like Andromeda are vast collections of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sirius:**

 
 
• Sirius, also known as the **Dog Star**, is the brightest star in the night sky. It is located in the constellation Canis Major.
 
• Sirius is a binary star system consisting of Sirius A and its faint companion, Sirius B.
 
• It is approximately **8.6 light-years** away from Earth, making it one of the closest stars to our planet.
 
• Sirius is not a galaxy but a star system.
 
 
 
• **Orion:**
 
 
• Orion is a prominent constellation visible from Earth, famous for the **Orion Belt**, which consists of three aligned stars.
 
• It contains notable stars like **Betelgeuse** and **Rigel**, and features the Orion Nebula, which is a stellar nursery.
 
• Orion is not a galaxy but a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern.
 
 
 
• **Ursa Minor:**
 
 
• Ursa Minor, or the **Little Bear**, is a constellation known for containing the **North Star** (Polaris), which is a key navigational star.
 
• It is located near the celestial north pole and is used to find direction in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• Ursa Minor is not a galaxy but a constellation.
 
 
 
• **Galaxies:**
 
 
• A galaxy is a massive system consisting of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.
 
• The Milky Way (our galaxy), Andromeda, and Triangulum are part of the Local Group of galaxies.
 
• Galaxies come in different types, such as **spiral, elliptical, and irregular**, each with unique characteristics and structures.
 
• Galaxies are studied to understand cosmic phenomena like star formation, black holes, and dark matter.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Andromeda-Milky Way Collision:**

 
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy is on a collision course with the Milky Way, predicted to occur in approximately **4.5 billion years**.
 
• This event will result in the formation of a new galaxy, sometimes referred to as **Milkomeda**.
 
 
 
• **Galactic Research:**
 
 
• Studying galaxies like Andromeda helps scientists understand cosmic evolution, including the formation and lifecycle of stars.
 
• Research on galaxies contributes to insights into phenomena such as **supermassive black holes** and the distribution of **dark matter**.

questions.question: What is the difference between displacement and distance?

options.text: Distance includes direction; displacement does not
Displacement includes direction; distance does not

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Displacement includes direction; distance does not**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 

• **Displacement** is a vector quantity that specifies the shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions of an object, along with the direction of movement. 

• **Distance**, on the other hand, is a scalar quantity that measures the total length of the path traveled by an object, irrespective of the direction. 

• Displacement can have a positive, negative, or zero value depending on the direction of motion, while distance is always positive and cannot be negative. 

• For example, if an object moves 10 meters forward and then 10 meters backward to its starting point, the displacement is 0 meters (due to no net change in position), while the distance is 20 meters. 

• Displacement considers direction and magnitude, making it more specific for indicating the change in position, whereas distance only measures magnitude, making it less specific. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Vector Quantity:** 

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, and force. 

• Displacement is a vector quantity because it specifies both the magnitude (shortest distance) and direction. 
 
 

• **Scalar Quantity:** 

• A scalar quantity has only magnitude and no direction. Examples include distance, speed, mass, and temperature. 

• Distance is a scalar quantity because it measures only the magnitude of the path traveled. 
 
 

• **Applications:** 

• Displacement is used in physics for calculations involving motion, such as determining velocity and acceleration. 

• Distance is commonly used for practical purposes like measuring travel lengths or determining road routes. 
 
 

• **Example:** 

• If a person walks 3 km north and then 4 km east, the distance traveled is 7 km, while the displacement (using Pythagoras theorem) is 5 km northeast. 

• This highlights the difference between the total path traveled (distance) and the shortest path between two points (displacement). 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Directional Significance:** Displacement’s inclusion of direction makes it crucial for vector-based calculations in physics, while distance is used for scalar measurements. 

• **Zero Displacement:** If an object returns to its starting point after movement, displacement is zero, but distance measures the total path traveled. 

• **Real-Life Scenarios:** Distance is practical for everyday usage (e.g., driving or running), while displacement is essential for scientific experiments and modeling motion. 

• **Geographical Representation:** In maps, displacement is represented as straight-line distance between two points, while distance considers the curved or actual traveled path.

questions.question: Under which article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Equality guaranteed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14 to Article 18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Equality** is guaranteed under **Articles 14 to 18** of the Indian Constitution. It is one of the fundamental rights provided to citizens of India.
 
• **Article 14:** Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This ensures no discrimination against individuals on any grounds.
 
• **Article 15:** Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. It also enables the state to make special provisions for women, children, and socially disadvantaged groups.
 
• **Article 16:** Ensures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. It prohibits discrimination in employment based on religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence.
 
• **Article 17:** Abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form. This article is a step towards eradicating caste-based discrimination in society.
 
• **Article 18:** Abolishes titles except for military and academic distinctions. It aims to prevent the creation of artificial hierarchies in Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, providing citizens with basic human rights essential for their development.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, ensuring protection against arbitrary actions by the state.
 
• They include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• **Article 14:**
 
 
• It emphasizes equality before the law, ensuring that every individual is subject to the same laws without favoritism.
 
• The concept of "equal protection of the laws" guarantees that individuals in similar circumstances will be treated equally.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:**
 
 
• It prohibits discrimination on specific grounds, fostering inclusivity and social justice.
 
• The state is empowered to make affirmative actions like reservations for disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Article 17:**
 
 
• This article is instrumental in abolishing untouchability, a social evil prevalent in India.
 
• It ensures that individuals belonging to the lower castes are treated equally and with dignity.
 
 
 
• **Article 18:**
 
 
• It prevents individuals from using titles that create social hierarchies, ensuring a classless society.
 
• Military and academic distinctions are exceptions under this article.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights vs Directive Principles:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by courts, while Directive Principles of State Policy are non-enforceable guidelines for governance.
 
• Both aim to establish a welfare state but differ in their legal binding nature.
 
 
 
• **Equality vs Equity:**
 
 
• Equality ensures equal treatment for all, while equity focuses on fairness and addressing disparities.
 
• Articles 15 and 16 incorporate elements of equity through affirmative actions like reservations.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in interpreting and safeguarding fundamental rights.
 
• Landmark cases like Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala reaffirm the importance of fundamental rights in India's constitutional framework.

• **Behavioral Change:** Encourages citizens to adopt hygiene practices such as handwashing and proper waste disposal.

• The **Stand-Up India Scheme** was launched by the **Government of India on April 5, 2016**, with the objective of promoting **entrepreneurship among women and Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST)**. 
 
• The scheme primarily provides **bank loans ranging from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore** to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up a greenfield enterprise. 
 
• The enterprise could be in the sectors of **manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities, or trading**. The main aim is to encourage economic participation from these underrepresented groups. 
 
• The scheme is implemented through all branches of **Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs)** across India, ensuring widespread accessibility. 
 
• It also provides **handholding support** by facilitating guidance, mentorship, and assistance with registration and other requirements.

• **Eligibility Criteria:** 
 
 
• The applicant must be a **woman or belong to the SC/ST category**. 
 
• The age of the borrower must be **above 18 years**. 
 
• The loans are specifically for **greenfield projects**, i.e., the first-time venture of the beneficiary in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors. 
 
• The borrower should not be in default to any bank or financial institution. 
 
 

 
• **Loan Details:** 
 
 
• The loan amount ranges from **Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore**. 
 
• The scheme provides a **composite loan** (inclusive of term loan and working capital) for setting up an enterprise. 
 
• The repayment period for the loan is up to **7 years**, with a maximum moratorium period of 18 months. 
 
 

 
• **Support System:** 
 
 
• The scheme includes a dedicated portal (**Stand-Up Mitra**) that offers handholding support and connects borrowers with banks and other stakeholders. 
 
• Mentorship and guidance are provided to help applicants with technical and financial expertise. 
 
 

 
• **Achievements:** 
 
 
• Since its inception in **2016**, the scheme has supported thousands of women and SC/ST entrepreneurs in setting up their businesses. 
 
• It has contributed significantly to **financial inclusion** and the empowerment of marginalized communities in India. 
 
 

 
• **Comparison with Other Schemes:** 
 
 
• Unlike schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana**, which focuses on micro-enterprises, the Stand-Up India Scheme specifically targets women and SC/ST entrepreneurs for medium-scale businesses. 
 
• It also ensures **social equity** by addressing the economic challenges faced by these groups. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Key Data:** As of **March 2023**, more than **1.5 lakh beneficiaries** have been sanctioned loans under the Stand-Up India Scheme, with a significant proportion being women entrepreneurs. 
 
• **Sectoral Focus:** The scheme encourages innovation and entrepreneurship in sectors like **manufacturing, services, and agriculture-allied activities**, driving economic growth in rural and urban areas.

questions.question: How has the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) improved healthcare services?

• **Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Healthcare:** AI has been widely adopted in healthcare to enhance diagnostic accuracy, improve treatment planning, and optimize patient care. By analyzing large datasets of medical records and imaging, AI systems can identify patterns and anomalies that may not be immediately apparent to human doctors. 

• **Accurate Diagnoses:** AI-powered tools like machine learning algorithms and neural networks analyze patient data, including symptoms, medical history, and test results, to provide precise and early diagnoses of diseases such as cancer, diabetes, and cardiovascular disorders. 

• **Data Analysis:** AI systems process vast amounts of data in real-time. For example, IBM Watson Health uses AI to sift through medical literature and case studies to recommend the most effective treatments for specific conditions. 

• **Predictive Analytics:** AI enables predictive analytics, helping healthcare providers forecast disease outbreaks, patient deterioration, and hospital resource utilization. This contributes to proactive healthcare measures and better patient outcomes. 

• **Examples:** AI applications such as Google's DeepMind are used in diagnosing eye diseases, while AI-based radiology systems interpret X-rays and MRIs with high precision. This significantly reduces diagnostic errors and ensures timely treatment. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__

• **Medical Imaging:** AI algorithms are used to analyze CT scans, MRIs, and mammograms for detecting abnormalities like tumors or fractures. 

• **Drug Discovery:** AI accelerates the drug development process by identifying potential drug candidates and predicting their efficacy. 

• **Virtual Health Assistants:** Chatbots and virtual assistants powered by AI provide patients with health-related information, appointment scheduling, and symptom checking. 

• **Robotic Surgery:** AI-driven robotic systems like the da Vinci Surgical System assist surgeons in performing minimally invasive procedures with precision. 

• **Personalized Medicine:** AI tailors treatment plans based on an individual’s genetic makeup, lifestyle, and medical history for more effective outcomes. 
 
 

• **Global Impact:** 
 

• Countries like the **United States**, **United Kingdom**, and **India** are integrating AI into their healthcare systems to improve efficiency and accessibility. 

• AI adoption in healthcare is projected to grow at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of **46.2%** between **2021** and **2027**, according to industry reports. 
 
 

• **Limitations:** 
 

• AI systems depend on the quality and quantity of data. Inaccurate or insufficient data can lead to errors in diagnosis or treatment recommendations. 

• Ethical concerns, such as patient data privacy and the potential for bias in AI algorithms, must be addressed to ensure fair and equitable healthcare delivery. 
 
 

• **AI vs. Human Expertise:** While AI enhances decision-making, it does not replace doctors. Human oversight remains essential for interpreting AI-generated insights and providing compassionate patient care.

questions.question:
A diver was swimming at a depth of -30 meters below sea level. She then ascended 18 meters towards the surface.

What is her new position relative to sea level?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial depth below sea level = −30 m

Movement (ascent) = +18 m

Final position = −30 + 18 = −12 m

The position is 12 meters below sea level.

**∴ Answer = 12 meters**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial position of the diver = 30 meters below sea level (−30 m)

Ascent distance = 18 meters (positive movement)

**Formula used:**

New Position = Initial Position + Upward Displacement

 
• Sea Level (0 m) 
• 
 Start: −30 m New Position: −12 m Ascent (+18 m) 
• Total Depth: 30 m 

**Calculations:**

The initial position is 30 meters below the surface, represented as −30.

⇒ New position = −30 + 18

⇒ New position = −12

⇒ The negative sign indicates it is below sea level, so the depth is 12 meters.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 meters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Integers and Sea Level

In mathematical problems, sea level is treated as the reference point zero (0). Positions above sea level are positive (+), and positions below sea level are negative (−).

Net Displacement

The final position is always the algebraic sum of the initial position and the changes. Displacement upward is added, while displacement downward is subtracted.

Absolute Value of Depth

The term 'depth' itself implies a distance below a surface. While the coordinate is −12, the depth is the absolute value |−12| = 12 meters.

questions.question: A factory uses 18.75 liters of a chemical each day. On Monday, it used only 2/3 of the daily amount. On Tuesday, it used 25% more than it did on Monday. How much chemical was used in total over the two days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Daily Usage = 18.75 liters

Monday usage = 2/3 of Daily

Tuesday usage = Monday × 1.25 = 2/3 × 5/4 = 5/6 of Daily

Total (Mon + Tue) = (2/3 + 5/6) × Daily = (4/6 + 5/6) × Daily = 9/6 × 18.75

Total = 1.5 × 18.75 = 28.125 liters

**∴ Answer = 28.125 liters**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Standard daily usage = 18.75 liters

Monday usage = 2/3 of standard usage

Tuesday usage = Monday usage + 25% of Monday usage

**Formula used:**

Amount = Base Value × Fraction/Percentage factor

Total Amount = Monday Amount + Tuesday Amount

 Daily Standard Usage: 18.75 L Monday (2/3 of 18.75) = 12.5 L Tuesday (125% of Monday) = 15.625 L 
• Total = 12.5 + 15.625 = 28.125 L 

**Calculations:**

Monday usage = 2/3 × 18.75

⇒ Monday usage = 2 × 6.25 = 12.5 liters

⇒ Tuesday usage = 12.5 + (25% of 12.5)

⇒ Tuesday usage = 12.5 + (0.25 × 12.5) = 12.5 + 3.125 = 15.625 liters

⇒ Total usage = 12.5 + 15.625

⇒ Total usage = 28.125 liters

**∴ The correct answer is 28.125 liters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert percentages to fractions: 25% = 1/4, 50% = 1/2, 75% = 3/4. Adding 25% is equivalent to multiplying by 5/4.

Successive Changes

If a value is changed by x% and then y%, the net change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%. For multi-step problems, applying factors (like 2/3 or 1.25) sequentially is most efficient.

Decimal Fraction Multiplication

When multiplying decimals like 1.5 × 18.75, treat it as 3/2 × 18.75 to make the division by 2 easier (9.375) then multiply by 3.

questions.question: How many natural numbers are there between 11² and 12²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The number of natural numbers between the squares of two consecutive numbers n² and (n + 1)² is always equal to 2n.

Comparing the given numbers 11² and 12² with n² and (n + 1)², we find n = 11.

Total natural numbers between them = 2 × 11 = 22.

**∴ Answer = 22**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lower limit = 11², Upper limit = 12²

**Formula used:**

Natural numbers between two values A and B = B − A − 1

 
• 11² (121) 12² (144) 22 Numbers (Excluding 121 and 144) 

**Calculations:**

First number (A) = 11² = 121

⇒ Second number (B) = 12² = 144

⇒ Numbers between 121 and 144 = 144 − 121 − 1

⇒ Numbers between = 23 − 1 = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

The difference between the squares of two consecutive natural numbers is equal to their sum: (n + 1)² − n² = (n + 1) + n = 2n + 1.

Sum of Odd Numbers

The square of any natural number n is equal to the sum of the first n odd natural numbers. For example, 3² = 1 + 3 + 5 = 9.

Non-Perfect Squares

The number of non-perfect square numbers between n² and (n + 1)² is given by 2n, where n is the smaller natural number.

questions.question: A recipe needs 3 cups of flour to make 12 muffins. How many cups of flour are needed to make 20 muffins in the same proportion?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Muffins to Flour ratio = 12 : 3 = 4 : 1

This means 4 muffins require 1 cup of flour.

Required flour for 20 muffins = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cups

**∴ Answer = 5 cups**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Flour₁ = 3 cups, Muffins₁ = 12

Muffins₂ = 20, Flour₂ = x

**Formula used:**

Direct Proportion: Flour₁ ÷ Muffins₁ = Flour₂ ÷ Muffins₂

 12 Muffins 3 Cups 20 Muffins x Cups 
• 
• Ratio: 12 ÷ 3 = 20 ÷ x 

**Calculations:**

Using the proportion method:

⇒ 3 ÷ 12 = x ÷ 20

⇒ 1 ÷ 4 = x ÷ 20

⇒ x = 20 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cups.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When two quantities increase or decrease together, they are in direct proportion. Formula: y = k × x or y₁/x₁ = y₂/x₂.

Inverse Proportion

When one quantity increases as the other decreases. Formula: x × y = k or x₁ × y₁ = x₂ × y₂.

Unitary Method

A technique where you first find the value of a single unit and then multiply by the required number of units.

 3 Students Total: 3 × 45 = 135 kg 1 Student 51 kg

questions.question: A solid cone is melted and recast into smaller cones of the same height but half the radius. How many smaller cones can be made?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the height of the cones remains constant, Volume is directly proportional to the square of the radius.

Radius of smaller cone = 1/2 of original radius.

Volume ratio = (Radius ratio)² = (1/2)² = 1/4.

The volume of each small cone is 1/4th of the original cone.

Number of cones = Original Volume ÷ New Volume = 1 ÷ (1/4) = 4.

**∴ Answer = 4**

⇒ V₂ = (1/3) × π × (R²/4) × H

⇒ V₂ = (1/4) × [(1/3) × π × R² × H] = V₁ / 4

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The teacher gave (1) / a advice (2) / which was really (3) / helpful(4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part (2)** of the sentence due to the incorrect use of the article "**a**" (or "an") with the word "**advice**."
 
• In English grammar, "**advice**" is an **uncountable noun**. Uncountable nouns represent things that cannot be counted as individual units and, therefore, do not take the indefinite articles "a" or "an."
 
• To correct this, you can either remove the article entirely, use "**some advice**," or use a partitive phrase like "**a piece of advice**."
 
• Thus, the phrase "a advice" is grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The teacher gave **some advice** which was really helpful."* (OR *"...gave **a piece of advice**..."*)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Uncountable Nouns:** Other words that follow this rule and cannot be used with "a/an" include: *Information, Furniture, Luggage, Baggage, News, Work, Knowledge,* and *Equipment*.
 
• **1: "The teacher gave"** – This is the subject and the simple past tense verb, which is correct.
 
• **3: "which was really"** – This relative clause correctly refers back to the advice. Since "advice" is uncountable, it is treated as singular, making "was" the correct verb.
 
• **4: "helpful"** – This is the adjective modifying the noun "advice," and it is used correctly here.
